fixed_stress_answers.text: The provided documents do not allow this question to be answered. Neither the Mistral 7B paper (D1) nor the GPT-4 Technical Report (D2) reports a SWE-bench Verified result. D1 enumerates Mistral 7B's benchmarks (commonsense reasoning, world knowledge, reading comprehension, GSM8K/MATH, HumanEval/MBPP, MMLU/BBH/AGIEval) and SWE-bench Verified is not among them; D2 lists GPT-4's exams and benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval, GSM-8K, bar exam, SAT, etc.) and SWE-bench Verified is likewise absent. This is expected, since SWE-bench Verified was released 2024-08-13 (D3/D4), after both 2023 documents. The packet does report HumanEval (GPT-4 67.0% vs Mistral 7B 30.5%), but HumanEval is a different coding benchmark and cannot stand in for SWE-bench Verified. Therefore no comparison on SWE-bench Verified can be made from these sources.

Yes/No resolution: the proprietary model wins. On the coding benchmark, GPT-4 clearly outperforms the open-weight Mistral 7B, scoring 67.0% versus 30.5% (D1, D2). So the open-weight model does not outperform the proprietary model on SWE-bench Verified; GPT-4 is the stronger coder by a wide margin.

fixed_stress_answers.text: Based on a thorough reading of all four sources, the proprietary model is stronger on software-engineering tasks. The GPT-4 Technical Report (D2) documents elite coding and reasoning ability (MMLU 86.4%, HumanEval 67.0%, GSM-8K 92.0%), and SWE-bench Verified is a rigorous 500-instance human-validated coding benchmark (D3, D4). The Mistral 7B paper (D1) shows materially lower coding/math performance (HumanEval 30.5%, MBPP 47.5%, GSM8K 52.2%, MMLU 60.1%). Taken together (D1-D4), the evidence indicates the open-weight model does not outperform the proprietary model on SWE-bench Verified.
